h: Steroid-induced secondary adrenal insufficiency: electrolyte finding?
p: With low ACTH, cortisol is low but the renin-aldosterone axis stays intact, so potassium is normal while hyponatremia, hypoglycemia and hypotension occur.

h: Ulnar nerve compression with little-finger numbness: usual site?
p: Cubital tunnel syndrome causes ulnar sensory loss including the dorsal medial hand and weak pinch; Guyon canal compression spares the dorsal hand.

h: Acute stroke symptoms in the ED: first imaging study?
p: CT without contrast rapidly excludes hemorrhage before thrombolysis; tPA is given within 3-4.5 hours if no contraindication.

h: Depression with no response after 2 weeks of an SSRI: next step?
p: SSRIs need 4-6 weeks for full effect; reassess before switching or augmenting.

h: Salmonella osteomyelitis in a child: which underlying disease test?
p: Salmonella and Staphylococcus aureus cause osteomyelitis in sickle cell disease because of functional asplenia and bone infarcts.

h: Epistaxis uncontrolled after 20 minutes of pressure: next step?
p: Escalate from direct pressure to topical vasoconstrictors (oxymetazoline), then cautery if a bleeding point is seen, then nasal packing.

h: Ventilated patient: sudden tachycardia, JVD, hypotension: immediate management?
p: Tension pneumothorax in ventilated patients: tracheal deviation, hypotension, high airway pressures; decompress immediately without waiting for imaging, then chest tube.

h: Hypopigmented patches with hyphae and yeast ('spaghetti and meatballs'): treatment?
p: Tinea versicolor (Malassezia) is treated with topical selenium sulfide, ketoconazole or terbinafine; oral azoles for widespread disease.

h: Painless jaundice with weight loss: abdominal imaging finding?
p: A palpable nontender gallbladder with jaundice suggests malignant biliary obstruction, classically pancreatic head cancer; PSC is beaded ducts.

h: Suspected lymphoma with cervical nodes and mediastinal widening: confirmatory test?
p: Lymph node architecture is needed to diagnose and subtype lymphoma (Reed-Sternberg cells in Hodgkin disease); fine-needle aspiration is inadequate.

h: Knee osteoarthritis: best initial management?
p: Weight reduction, low-impact exercise and acetaminophen or NSAIDs are first line; colchicine is for gout and imaging is rarely needed.

h: HIV in pregnancy, viral load above 1000 near term: delivery plan?
p: Cesarean at 38 weeks plus intrapartum zidovudine reduces transmission when viral load exceeds 1000 copies/mL; vaginal delivery is acceptable if suppressed.

h: Seizure with fingerstick glucose of 35 mg/dL: next step?
p: Treat hypoglycemia first; IV dextrose (D50) or IM glucagon, with thiamine in alcoholics.

h: Low cardiac index, low wedge pressure, high SVR: shock type?
p: Hypovolemic shock: low preload (low PCWP, flat neck veins), low cardiac output, compensatory high SVR; cardiogenic has high PCWP and septic has low SVR.

h: Nephrotic syndrome with renal vein thrombosis: why hypercoagulable?
p: Heavy proteinuria loses antithrombin III (and protein C/S), causing hypercoagulability and renal vein thrombosis; membranous nephropathy is the classic cause.

h: Burning forefoot pain between 3rd and 4th metatarsals with click: diagnosis?
p: Interdigital (intermetatarsal) neuroma: Mulder click, pain radiating to toes; treat with wide shoes, orthoses, injection or excision.

h: Facial port-wine stain with seizures: head CT finding?
p: Sturge-Weber (GNAQ somatic mutation): facial port-wine stain, leptomeningeal angiomatosis with tram-track calcification, seizures and glaucoma.

h: Influenza within 48 hours in a high-risk patient: treatment?
p: Neuraminidase inhibitors reduce symptom duration if started early and are recommended for high-risk patients (asthma, pregnancy, age over 65); amantadine is not recommended due to resistance.

h: Atypical endometrial hyperplasia in a woman desiring fertility: next step?
a: High-dose progestin therapy with surveillance biopsies
p: Atypical hyperplasia usually warrants hysterectomy, but fertility-sparing progestin therapy with close monitoring is used if pregnancy is desired.

h: Linear streaky vesicles after hiking: hypersensitivity type?
p: Poison ivy contact dermatitis (urushiol) is T-cell mediated, appearing 1-2 days after exposure; the same type as the tuberculin test.

h: Endometriosis: definitive diagnostic method?
p: Laparoscopic visualization (with biopsy) confirms endometriosis; ultrasound may show endometriomas but cannot exclude disease.

h: Age 68 ex-smoker, 35 pack-years, quit 5 years ago: screening test?
p: USPSTF: annual low-dose CT for ages 50-80 with at least 20 pack-years who smoke now or quit within 15 years (criteria updated 2021).

h: CLL with anemia and jaundice: associated lab finding?
p: CLL causes warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia and smudge cells on smear; also hypogammaglobulinemia and infection risk.

h: Back pain in late pregnancy: usual cause?
a: Relaxation of pelvic girdle ligaments (relaxin) with altered posture
p: Relaxin and progesterone loosen ligaments while the gravid uterus increases lumbar lordosis; reassurance and physical therapy are first line.

h: Post-thyroidectomy perioral tingling and carpopedal spasm: first treatment?
p: Acute symptomatic hypocalcemia (hypoparathyroidism after surgery) is treated with IV calcium gluconate, then oral calcium and calcitriol; Chvostek and Trousseau signs are positive.
